title: Backtest: 'The strait is officially open, go short Brent'

input.event: The Strait of Hormuz is officially open again, so go short Brent

allowed_exceptions.hz-004: PortWatch methodology; the excerpt date is the retrieval date (2026-08-25) but the content was public before as_of
allowed_exceptions.hz-006: same as hz-004 (weekly Tuesday updates, so data lags)
allowed_exceptions.hz-009: excerpt date is the retrieval date (2026-10-14); content is the 2025 and Feb 2026 pre-closure baseline, public well before as_of
allowed_exceptions.hz-010: excerpt date is the retrieval date (2026-10-14); content is 4/9-4/28 transits, published weekly, visible by early May

excluded.hz-016: mixes pre- and post-decision information in one excerpt; needs splitting by the evidence line

outcome.truth: Transits from 6/18 to 7/8 averaged about 24 ships/day with a peak of 51 on 6/24, under half the pre-closure ~92 (hz-011); the IRGC declared the strait closed again on 7/12 (hz-012); Brent fell to $69 on 7/2 and was back at $105 on 7/23 (hz-019).

observations.note: Only the peak is a single-day value; the ~24/day average is a range mean and cannot be a daily record. Full daily data needs a PortWatch export from the evidence line.
JMIC advisory declaring the strait open (hz-008). A fact before the decision date, included so conditions about the notice can be judged.

outcome.matching_note: Conditions are matched to outcome data by name or alias first, then by the match keywords against the condition's series, source and rule text (same kind only). Unmatched conditions go to human review, not FAIL.

expected.behavior: Do not treat the 6/20 reopening notice as an entry signal. The key dependency is sustained real transits; cite the hz-009 pre-closure baseline and leave the recovery threshold to the user (null threshold plus a note). Address the hz-010 precedent (no recovery after the April ceasefire). Exit conditions include an observable event such as a renewed closure or new attack.
expected.key_dependency_should_be: sustained recovery of real transits, not the reopening notice

backtest.entry_resolution: Depends on the user-confirmed threshold: above 51 ships/day the entry condition is never met from 6/18 to 7/8 (avoiding the July reversal); at or below 51 it is met on 6/24

exit_should_trigger.what: renewed closure / new blockade or attack

contamination_probe: Without any documents: what happened in the Strait of Hormuz in July 2026, after it was declared open on June 20, 2026? How did Brent move?
human_review: Backtest: is the key dependency real transits or the reopening notice
E1: are hz-010 and hz-015 addressed
E2: could the exit conditions fire on 7/12
notes: Backtests must run offline: the runner refuses --online for layer R; the pack holds only allowed_excerpts, outcome excerpts are used for grading only; the contamination probe runs first; citing anything outside allowed_excerpts counts as a leak.
pack_rule: Point-in-time pack = every excerpt public by as_of, not just the relevant ones: the product puts the whole pack in context, so hand-picking would make the task easier than reality.
